full_judgment:
2. The plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration that the orders of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong passed on 4-4-1984 in Settlement Appeal Case No. 154 of 1981-82 cancelling the S2ttlement of the suit land made earlier in favour of the plaintiffs and the order dated 9-10-1985 passed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong in Settlement Revision Case No. 73 of 1984 affirming the orders of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong are illegal, ineffective, void and without jurisdiction and the plaintiffs and the suit properties are not bound by the same and for further declaration that the judgment and orders dated 23-6-1981 passed in settlement appeal Nos. 228, 229 and 243 of 1979-80 and settlement Revision No. 168 of 1981 on 14-11-1982 by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong and Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong were legal, justified, effective and correct and that the plaintiffs sought for further declaration of their title and possession in the suit land under the Government. That the plaintiffs stated, inter alia that 12.95 stakes of land of RS Plot Nos. 1732 and 1733 of Mouza Ghunia, Police Station Chakaria, District Cox's Bazar belonged to Government and on whose behalf local Thana Revenue Officer manages the land. The land were fallow and that the plaintiffs hailing from the same Mouza are landless cultivators and they applied to the local revenue officer for settlement of the suit land and by dint of labour and spending money made the land cultivable and enjoyed the same producing paddy and during inquiry they were found in possession by the local Tasilder, who submitted proposal for settlement of the property in their name and the Settlement Case Nos. 111-119 of 1978 were started and thereafter invited objections and then the proposals were thus initiated. The defendant Nos. 1-15 filed objection illegally and their objections were heard by the then Sub-Divisional Officer, who rejected their objections on 13-9-1981; the SDO, Cox's Bazar ultimately approved the proposals in favour of the plaintiff and settled the property for a period of 15 years and that the plaintiffs paid compensation for their back possession and rents and that defendant Nos. 1-15 being greedy persons filed objections and appeals before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong who rejected their objections. The order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong was affirmed up to the Court of Divisional Commissioner and that the aforesaid defendants being unable to grab the properties filed objections repeatedly before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong. The defendants again filed Settlement Appeal No. 154 of 1981-82 for cancellation of the approval given by the SDO on 13-9-81 in favour of the plaintiffs, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong after hearing the parties by his order dated 4-4-1984 allowed the appeal. Thereafter, the plaintiffs preferred Settlement Revision Case No. 73 of 1984 before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong, who by his order dated 9-10-1985 affirmed the aforesaid order dated 4-4-1985 of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong. That the plaintiffs further stated that the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong had no jurisdiction to pass the order on 4-4-1984 as at that time Cox's Bazar became a separate District from 1-3-1984 and the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division also committed an error of law in affirming the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, who passed the order beyond his territorial jurisdiction and that the orders are illegal and ineffective and that the local Revenue Officer has been trying to lease out the suit property to other persons on the strength of the aforesaid illegal orders and hence the plaintiffs felt constrained to institute the suit. 

 3. That the defendant Nos. 1-15, 19 and 20-26 submitted separate written statements but during the hearing only defendant No. 19 and defendant Nos. 20-26 contested the suit. 

 4. That the defendant No. 19 (Government) contested the suit stating, inter alia, that the suit properties are Government khas land and though the properties were leased in favour of the plaintiffs but at the instance of the defendants the settlement Appeal No. 154 of 1981-82 was filed and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Chittagong cancelled the proposals on the basis of materials on record and settlement revision No. 73 of 1984 filed before Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong was also rejected on hearing the parties. There being provisions of appeals before the higher forums, the plaintiffs did not exhaust the same. The plaintiffs have no right, title or possession in the suit land. The suit is barred under section 76(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The property stands recorded in Khas Khatian of the Government. The suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 5. The added defendant Nos. 20-26 filed the written statements denying the case of the plaintiffs and stating, inter alia, that the suit has been filed collusively by the plaintiffs and the defendants Nos. 1-15, and that the suit is not maintainable and that the defendants being Member of Kakara Mini-Bazar Bittihin Samabaya Samity are in physical possession of the suit land and that the suit has not been properly valued and that the suit lands are collusion lands from the River Matamuhuri and suncrops are produced there and that the defendants getting the land on 'eksana' basis have been in physical possession of the suit land and that the plaintiffs in collusion with the defendant Nos. 1-15 collusively tried to get the suit land settled secretly and that then the added defendants and others filed Settlement Appeal before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong and the settlement having not been finalised and approved, their appeals were found premature and the appeals were dismissed and that after approval of the settlement cases, the petitioner and others filed settlement appeal No. 154 of 1981-42 and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Chittagong cancelled the settlement as it was found that the plaintiffs are not eligible nor the lands are fit to be settled as raiyatwari settlement as it was not fit for producing paddy and there was misrepresentation of fact as to the nature of land. The order of Additional Deputy Commissioner was affirmed by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong in settlement Revision No. 136 of 1985 and an appeal before the Board of Land Administration, Dhaka by forging the judgment of the Commissioner's Court was preferred but the forgery being detected, the Board "filed" the appeal and directed to refer the matter to Anti-Corruption which is pending and that by suppression of those facts, the plaintiffs collusively filed the instant suit and that the suit itself is fraudulent and malafide as the plaintiffs with oblique motive did not implead the added defendants and that plaintiff No. 2 Ali Akbar instituted a few false criminal cases against the added defendants wherein the defendant Nos. 1-15 have been cited as witness and that the plaintiff No. 2 Ali Akbar and the defendant No. 1 Kamaluddin jointly filed objection against the added defendants regarding the suit land to the local Upazila Chairman, which ipso facto proves the unholy collusion of the plaintiffs and the defendants Nos. 1-15. The defendants further stated that, in view of the orders of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong cancelling the settlements proposals in the names of the plaintiffs and since no agreement was executed between the parties, no Jamabandi Khatians being created in the names of the plaintiffs, they have no right, title or possession over the suit property nor they have any locus standi to file or maintain the suit and that the suit is liable to be dismissed having no cause of action. 

 7. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the petitioners, submits that the Court of appeal below found that due to the litigation the lease deed could not be executed and registered which is a mere formality as the settlement was approved by the Sub-Divisional Officer in view of the policy of the Government vide clause 8 of GO No. 21-72/70/223-RL dated 2nd August 1972 made under the provision of section 76(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, High Court Division erred in law in taking exception as to non-compliance of the requirement of section 81B of the Act. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that in view of creation of a new district of Cox's Bazar with effect from 1st March, 1984 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) had no territorial jurisdiction in passing the aforesaid order dated 4-4-1984 in Settlement Appeal Case No. 185 of 1981-82 and in view of that legal position, the jurisdiction of Civil Court is not ousted as the Civil Court has the plenary power of scrutiny as to whether the authority so created, travels beyond its jurisdiction and, as such, the suit was maintainable. 

 8. The High Court Division as it appears from the impugned judgment has considered the said G.O. dated 2nd April 1982 and held that neither G.O. nor the implementation clause had anything to show that the same could supersede the provision of section 81B of the said Act which must be complied with in leasing out agricultural khas land and in that respect section 76(2) of the said Act impliedly provided that Government is the highest authority to pass any order as to the settlement and Civil Court could not interefere with the same unless the same is malafide and coram non judice. Admittedly, no lease deed was executed so as to confer any legal right in the plaintiffs. Memorandum issued by the Government and the Rules relating to the settlement incorporated in the Government Estate Manual have no statutory force but merely provide guidelines and cannot be invoked for claiming a legal right. Similarly, the Court would be far exceeding its function if it were to assume jurisdiction to enforce performance of statutory duties by the public functionaries unless person who comes before the Court has an enforceable legal right. Thus one could only avail of the forum of the Civil Court for enforcement of any legal right or to redress the violation thereof.
